scope: Rear destruction correction and left/right/both fork storyboards

prompts.prompt: Use case: temporal game storyboard. Original coarse pixel-art graphics in the 1994 Doom II software-renderer aesthetic, matching the supplied image: chunky visible square pixels, gritty indexed brown stone and brick textures, strong dark distance bands, flat sector-style lighting, simple low-poly arches, no smooth painting, no bloom, no motion blur. Soot-black steam locomotive has circular FRONT boiler, two yellow lamps and cowcatcher, facing the viewer. Camera ahead of and above train looking BACK at its nose; the nose points toward BOTTOM of screen. A short locomotive, no long wagons. Train remains the SAME SIZE, centered at 58% image height in every frame, taking 24% of panel width, leaving clear foreground below and space behind above. Exactly three railway lanes where the corridor is straight. CRUCIAL spatial rule: scenery destruction occurs BEHIND the train, in the UPPER/MIDDLE background beyond its rear cab, NOT in front of its nose. Track and vault behind the train crack, drop bricks and sleepers, and collapse into glowing lava, growing across time. The safe route IN FRONT of train in LOWER foreground is always physically supported with continuous rails. Show both collapsing floor and falling broken arch sections behind the train. Never put the locomotive on lava or unsupported rail. Keep destruction separated from train by a short intact buffer. SAME fixed camera and consistent brick tunnel across sequential frames, not unrelated scene variants. Upper background is travelled route; bottom is approaching route. Number each panel with tiny white digits in a black upper-left corner tab, no other text, no HUD. SQUARE OUTPUT CANVAS with strict THREE COLUMNS by TWO ROWS, six equal portrait panels separated by thin black gutters. Revise the supplied scene into SIX consecutive storyboard phases of a STRAIGHT tunnel ride with collapsing world behind the train. Panels 01 02 03 on upper row, 04 05 06 lower row. 01: near brick arch overhead, distant cracks in the track BEHIND train and small glowing fissures in distant arch. 02: that distant track segment breaks and several stones fall, nearby safe foreground sleepers move upward. 03: a clear lava hole opens behind train and one far arch loses its keystone, angular blocks visibly falling. 04: collapse front follows behind train with a safe short buffer, old rails hang into the hole in upper-middle background, next intact arch enters at outer edge. 05: rubble sinks into lava behind, more of the rear tunnel vault crumbles, side walls behind reveal red-orange molten rock. 06: new intact near arch frames the train and intact foreground lanes, broad lava breach and disintegrating arch remain BEHIND train in upper half. Preserve locomotive silhouette, position and scale in ALL SIX panels. Only environment recedes towards vanishing point and breaks in the wake. Large readable pixel chunks; don't obscure train or approaching tracks with particles. This is not a loop resetting destroyed ground; it is a moving trail of collapse following the locomotive.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Convert the supplied THREE-FRAME LEFT-TURN railway tunnel storyboard into the corresponding THREE-FRAME RIGHT-TURN storyboard. Preserve landscape 3:2 canvas and three panels arranged horizontally, left-to-right temporal order 01,02,03. Within EACH individual panel mirror the entire scene horizontally so the vaulted side tunnel and safe curved rail route appear on SCREEN-RIGHT and the collapsed rear old route shifts to SCREEN-LEFT. The two signs must now show bright green RIGHT-pointing chevrons. Do NOT reverse the order of the three panels, and keep the frame labels in upper-left corners upright readable '01','02','03' (not mirrored). Front of steam locomotive still faces viewer in every frame, train stays roughly same size and central position. Preserve exact coarse chunky pixel texture resolution, same gritty brown Doom II-era software-rendered architecture, low resolution jagged details, orange lava and black cables. Frame01 approach RIGHT branch with incipient cracks BEHIND train, frame02 enter RIGHT branch with masonry and track breaking behind, frame03 intact RIGHT-curving selected path and old passed left/rear junction dropping into lava BEHIND train. The foreground path under and in front of train is always intact. No extra exits, no text besides frame numbers, no smooth rendering. This is the matched right-hand version of the same storyboard.
